name: type-coercion
description: Find type coercion bugs in calculations

promptLevels.beginner: find the type coercion bugs in the calculateTotal and applyDiscount functions
promptLevels.intermediate: analyze the code and identify where strings are being used in place of numbers, causing type coercion bugs in mathematical operations

languageInstructions.typescript: Provide a detailed bug analysis as a markdown document or structured response. Explain how TypeScript's strict mode, proper type annotations without 'as any', and compile-time checks would catch these bugs. Include corrected code examples with proper types and validation.
languageInstructions.javascript: Provide a detailed analysis explaining each bug and how it manifests in JavaScript's loose typing system. Include corrected code with proper type checking (using typeof, Number(), parseInt(), etc.) and validation before arithmetic operations.
languageInstructions.javascript-jsdoc: Provide analysis explaining how JSDoc type annotations could help catch these bugs during development (with IDE support) even though they don't provide runtime safety. Include corrected code with both JSDoc annotations and runtime validation.

performanceBenchmarks.name: type-checking-operations
performanceBenchmarks.code: const values = ["1", 1, "2", 2, "3", 3]; for (let i = 0; i < 10000; i++) { values.forEach(v => typeof v === "number"); }

performanceBenchmarks.name: type-conversion
performanceBenchmarks.code: const strings = Array.from({length: 1000}, (_, i) => String(i)); for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) { strings.map(s => Number(s)); }
